claims.claim: RuntimeConfig reuses `Provider` type from pkg/config
RuntimeConfig reuses `ToolSpec` type from pkg/config
RuntimeConfig reuses `MCPServerConfig` type from pkg/config
RuntimeConfig reuses `StateStoreConfig` type from pkg/config
RuntimeConfig reuses `LoggingConfigSpec` type from pkg/config
There is a programmatic option `WithRuntimeConfig()` that accepts configuration files
Options applied after WithRuntimeConfig() take precedence over YAML-declared settings

WithProvider, WithStateStore and WithLogger win on either side of WithRuntimeConfig; the file applies state store and logger only when none is set, a declared provider joins the pool; MCP servers append; exec eval bindings register into the eval registry and WithEvalRegistry after replaces it; exec tool bindings always apply
Tools, evals, and hooks can be implemented as external subprocesses in any language
One-shot (exec) mode spawns a new process for each invocation
One-shot mode: runtime passes input as JSON on stdin and reads result from stdout

Server mode keeps a long-running process, talks JSON-RPC 2.0 one object per line with method `execute`, matches replies to calls by id, drops a canceled call's late reply, and starts a new process if it exited
Server mode amortizes startup cost and allows subprocess to maintain state between invocations
Tool exec bindings (command, runtime, args, env) are configured entirely in RuntimeConfig; command is passed to the OS unchanged, not resolved against the config file
Exec bindings live in RuntimeConfig (operator-controlled), not in pack
`env` field in RuntimeConfig passes variable names, not values; actual values come from process environment at runtime
An exec tool binding's timeout_ms, when set, overrides the tool descriptor's timeout, which the registry defaults to 30 seconds

Registry wraps each call in a deadline, kills a one-shot process past it, returns a 'tool execution timed out' error to the LLM; in server mode the deadline abandons the call and the process keeps running
Documentation page exists at /sdk/how-to/conversations/use-runtime-config/
A one-shot exec tool can answer {"pending": ...}, which holds the call until the host supplies its result
